solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Painful experience when river floods holiday site?

indicators.note: a river flooding a site pours into it, so the river's letter goes inside

parts.note: a camp is a place to stay on holiday

explanation.surface: A holiday campsite inundated by a river would be a painful experience for the campers.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle spasm is a sharply painful thing to undergo, hence a painful experience.

clue.text: Start to chop wood for money

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of chop

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Chopping wood to earn some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins are ready money, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Intentions of excellent modern miss

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; written with the digit read as the letter I it gives AI
Ms is the modern title for a woman, replacing Miss

explanation.surface: What a fine young woman of today means to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is treated as the letters A and I, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Goals or purposes are what one intends, plural synonym of intentions.

clue.text: Funny last words in old magazine leading to row

indicators.note: the magazine comes first, ahead of the row

parts.note: Punch was a long-running British humour magazine, now defunct
a line is a row of people or things

explanation.surface: Something in an old humour magazine that sparked a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel but here means a line; PUNCH is a famous British satirical weekly that closed in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing line of a joke is what delivers the laugh, the comic final words.

clue.text: Party female, university learner looking embarrassed

parts.note: a bash is an informal party
L is for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A female student at a party looking embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and easily abashed, a near synonym for awkwardly self-conscious.

clue.text: Actor Richard seen in Staffs town

definitions.meaning: the Welsh film star Richard of Cleopatra fame, married to Elizabeth Taylor
Staffs is short for Staffordshire, an English county whose brewing town on the Trent carries this name

explanation.surface: A famous actor spotted in a Staffordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffs is the abbreviation for Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands; the town is Burton upon Trent, known for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the surname: Richard the actor, and the Staffordshire brewing town.

clue.text: It was written thus, sounding bad

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, so we take one sounding the same

parts.note: feeling bad means feeling ill or sick

explanation.surface: A remark about something written that came out sounding poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag inserted in quotations means 'thus', flagging that the original was written so.

clue.text: Something that's pink or bright red, a circular shape

parts.note: flaming describes a blazing red colour
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Describing a colour that is either pink or vivid red, with a ring shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-legged wading bird is famously pink, so it is something pink.

clue.text: What could be ale — demon drink

indicators.note: says the letters could be made into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Pondering what beer might become, calling it the demon drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demon drink' is a stock phrase for alcohol, but this drink is soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft beverage is a kind of drink.

clue.text: "Sir", name possibly used in class

indicators.note: suggests the letters might possibly be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pupil addressing the teacher as 'Sir' in class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial group in a university is a class for discussion.

clue.text: Delight shown by member joining church

indicators.note: the member is attached to the church, coming after it

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: The pleasure a new member shows on joining a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or captivate someone is to delight them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Goliath, one troubling student of religion

indicators.note: troubling the letters stirs them up into a new order

explanation.surface: The giant Goliath bothering someone who studies religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of divinity studies religion professionally.

clue.text: Inner group of moral politicians will appear in places of worship

indicators.note: the inner group of letters of moral, without its outer ones

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An inner circle of upright politicians turning up at churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Small chapels for private prayer are places of worship.

clue.text: Problem when spiteful female comes round for gossip

indicators.note: the female surrounds the problem, enclosing it

parts.note: a cat is slang for a spiteful woman
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A nasty woman calling by turns into a problem when she gossips.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle light conversation is a synonym for gossip.

clue.text: Most harsh task — rest after working

indicators.note: letters at work are being rearranged, set in a new order

explanation.surface: A really tough job, with a break only once the work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of stark, meaning bleakest or severest, matches most harsh.

clue.text: Erotic song that's supposed to impress listeners

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for empty boastful talk, a noun phrase

parts.note: hot can mean sexy or erotic
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A racy song meant to win over an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, boastful talk is meant to impress those listening but has no substance.

clue.text: Teased for wearing tatty clothes

definitions.meaning: past tense of rag, to tease or mock
dressed in torn and frayed garments

explanation.surface: Someone mocked for dressing shabbily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragging someone is teasing them; a person in tattered clothes looks frayed and torn.

clue.text: Underground water reportedly doesn't move

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so we want a word sounding alike

parts.note: the Styx is the river of the Greek underworld

explanation.surface: A report that water below ground stays still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' means the underworld of Greek myth, not a subterranean stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to stay fixed in place, so it stays put.

clue.text: Left-winger joining country dance

indicators.note: the left-winger is attached after the country

parts.note: Turkey is a nation straddling Europe and Asia
a Trot is short for Trotskyist, a far-left radical

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician aligning with a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtime-era ballroom step of the early twentieth century, a kind of dance.

clue.text: Old rodent climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: An aged rat scaling a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical root crop grown for its starchy tuber is a plant.

clue.text: Sunken shaft in good condition

definitions.meaning: a hole bored into the ground to reach water

explanation.surface: A shaft dug into the ground still in fine working order.
explanation.definitionFit: A water shaft dug into the earth, and the adjective for being healthy.

clue.text: More than one cad gets better, we hear

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken, so one of the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a wound that heals gets better

explanation.surface: A bunch of rotters improving their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is slang for a dishonourable man, so the plural covers several cads.

clue.text: Star celebrated endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: sung as in praised in song, celebrated

explanation.surface: A famous celebrity praised without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Our solar system's centre is a star.

clue.text: Greek character gets corporal punishment for trick

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the cane, a stick for beating, was a school punishment

explanation.surface: A Greek man being beaten for deceiving people.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is deceit, and the noun it comes from means a dodge or deception.

clue.text: Disease set aunt into a spin

indicators.note: sends the letters spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: An illness that threw a relative into a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw, a bacterial infection, is a serious disease.

clue.text: Person goes round far end of the capital city

indicators.note: the person surrounds the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone travelling around the remotest part of a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Korean seat of government is a capital city.
